name: Tennant Creek
reason: Sizable settlement and regional hub with a Wikivoyage guide-city page and NT tourism chapter; a destination candidate, not a spot.

reason: 2 counted sources, 5147 page views

name: Devils Marbles
reason: 3 counted sources, 14079 page views

name: The Pebbles
reason: 2 counted sources, 3135 page views

name: Tennant Creek Telegraph Station
reason: 3 counted sources, 435 page views

name: Nyinkka Nyunyu Art and Culture Centre
reason: Counted by Wikivoyage and NT tourism ('one of the best in the NT'); Warumungu art and interpretive exhibits, a visit of an hour (visitor-attraction, entry fee).

name: Battery Hill Mining Centre
reason: NT tourism's top-10 lists it: underground tour and Australia's last operating ten-head stamp battery, a real 1-2 hour visit.

name: Tennant Creek Museum
reason: Wikivoyage lists it: WWII hospital building with gold-rush exhibits, entry fee, a 30-60 min visit. Single counted source.

name: Winanjjikari Music Centre
reason: Wikivoyage invites visitors to watch musicians and join a song, free; an unusual cultural stop.

name: Bill Allen Lookout
reason: Wikivoyage names it, 360-degree sunset view just east of town.

name: Lake Mary Ann
reason: 3 counted sources, 733 page views

name: Warrego Fossicking Area
reason: An activity needing a permit and a tag-along tour rather than a place with something to see or do on arrival (rule 2).

name: Banka Banka Station
reason: Wikivoyage names it twice (Do and Go next): historic mud-brick homestead, campground, station life slide show in season.

name: Iytwelepenty / Davenport Range National Park
reason: 4 counted sources, 704 page views

name: Old Police Station Waterhole
reason: Four-wheel-drive swimming waterhole named as Davenport Range NP's best-known attraction by Wikivoyage and Parks NT; a real swim and camp stop.

name: Wycliffe Well
reason: 2 counted sources, 6947 page views

name: Lake Wycliffe
reason: A small man-made 10-acre lake beside a roadhouse; one Wikivoyage mention, ordinary pull-in (rule 3).

name: Wycliffe Well Railway
reason: A static relocated sugar-cane train beside a roadhouse; a ten-minute look, no guide singles it out.

name: Barrow Creek Telegraph Station
reason: NT Government (agency) information sheet: 1872 stone station reserve with a self-guided walk through the original buildings; free, open access; also listed on Wikivoyage Go next as Barrow Creek.

name: Barrow Creek Hotel
reason: accommodation

name: Barrow Creek
reason: A settlement of a roadhouse and pub; the town as such is not a draw, and the telegraph station is covered separately. No counted source names the town as a place to go beyond the Go next note.

name: Threeways Roadhouse
reason: A roadhouse junction with no counted source; the road-train mural is a minor photo stop.

name: Renner Springs
reason: NT tourism names it with a short lagoon and springs walk; Wikivoyage covers its telegraph history.

name: Newcastle Waters
reason: Ghost town with preserved historic buildings (Jones's Store, Junction Hotel) and Drovers Memorial Park; named by both Wikivoyage Go next and NT tourism.

name: Elliott
reason: A service town on the Stuart Highway (post office, police, clinic); no sights named for a visitor.

name: Attack Creek Historical Reserve
reason: Named by NT tourism top-10 and Wikivoyage; free reserve with Stuart cairn and etchings 74 km north.

name: Barkly Homestead
reason: A roadhouse and caravan park service stop; no counted source names it as a place to go.

name: Heartbreak Hotel
reason: accommodation

name: Cape Crawford Lost City
reason: NT tourism describes the Cape Crawford Lost City (20-mile-long sandstone pillars, canyons, arches); a distinct landscape draw in Limmen NP, with a helicopter flight and ground tour from Heartbreak Hotel (seasonal Apr-Oct). Pin must be taken from the Lost City itself not the Limmen centroid.

name: Connells Lagoon Conservation Reserve
reason: NT tourism's top-10 #10: rare birds in a wetland reserve, 2WD access by unsealed road.

name: Brunette Downs
reason: A 12,000 km2 cattle station with no public visitor facilities; a station is not a place to go (rule 2).

name: Anmatjere Man
reason: Quirky roadside icon: a giant steel sculpture visible from the Stuart Highway at Aileron, described on the NT tourism Aileron page; Aileron's roadhouse stop.

name: Ti-Tree
reason: A small service town (roadhouse and store) with no sights named by a visitor source.
